prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down outdoor construction scene where the camera wearer stands straddling a low, curved brick-and-mortar wall (~0.3–0.5 m high, ~1.0–1.5 m away on the ground), with their own torso, arms, hands, and legs appearing brightest in the lower foreground (~0.2–1.2 m away). In Frame 2, as the camera tilts slightly up, a second person's legs and a mortar pan held at their waist appear in the upper-right at ~2.0–2.5 m distance, facing toward the camera wearer while their upper body and head are cropped out of the top of the frame, alongside bricks and a round pan resting on the dirt ~1.5–1.8 m away. In Frame 3, the wearer extends both arms forward and upward (~0.3–0.7 m from the camera) to receive the round pan of wet mortar within arm's reach, which partly occludes the ground and lower legs behind it, before lowering the pan in Frame 4 (~0.6–0.9 m) and tipping it over the brick wall on the right in Frame 5 (~0.7–1.0 m) while holding a trowel in the right hand. Compared to RGB, the depth map more clearly separates the raised foreground arms, hands, and mortar pan from the similarly coloured brown dirt, bricks, and wet mortar below, and reveals the raised elevation profile of the curved masonry wall in Frames 1, 4, and 5. However, the depth map is unreliable in Frame 2 where the distant co-worker's legs and pan at the top right are rendered anomalously bright (as if closer than the mid-ground bricks), and in Frame 3 where the dark mortar pan held right in front of the hands appears much darker (farther) than the hands gripping its rim.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects only a sparse subset of foreground regions across the five frames, leaving most of the scene—including the ground, loose bricks, trowel, and the entirety of Frame 1—completely unsegmented in black. In Frame 2, it outlines the approaching co-worker's lower legs and pan at the top right (~2.0–2.5 m away, facing the wearer with their upper body out of view) as 'person' and 'sandwich', while labeling the curved brick-and-mortar wall at the bottom left (~1.2 m away) as 'sandwich' and the wearer's right hand holding the trowel (~0.6 m away) as 'person'. In Frame 3, it segments only the wearer's right forearm and hand reaching up at ~0.5 m as 'person' (missing the raised left arm and the mortar pan entirely), and in Frame 4 it segments a rock at the top left as 'carrot', the wearer's left leg (~1.2 m) as 'knife', and the lowered mortar pan held in both hands (~0.7 m) as 'broccoli'. In Frame 5, it captures the wearer's left leg on the left (~1.2 m), the mortar pan and arms at the bottom right (~0.7 m), and the right hand/arm on the far right (~0.6 m) as three separate 'person' masks. While the masks roughly localize a few key foreground contours (such as the co-worker's legs in Frame 2, the held pan in Frame 4, and the wearer's limbs in Frames 3–5), the map is highly unreliable due to severe COCO class hallucinations ('sandwich', 'carrot', 'broccoli', 'knife') and misses most objects and body parts visible in the RGB strip.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank (solid black) across all five frames, failing to detect any body joints or hand keypoints for either the camera wearer or the second person. In the RGB strip, the camera wearer's lower legs and feet straddling the low brick wall (~1.2–1.5 m below the head-mounted camera) and their arms and hands manipulating a trowel and a round mortar pan within arm's reach (~0.3–1.0 m in front and below) are clearly visible across Frames 1 to 5, as are the approaching co-worker's lower legs and hands holding the pan at ~2.0–2.5 m in Frame 2. Because both individuals are heavily truncated by the egocentric framing—with the camera wearer viewed steeply from above and the co-worker cropped above the waist so neither person's head or gaze is in view—and the hands are partially occluded by the trowel and mortar pan rim, the pose estimator fails to trigger. Consequently, the pose map contributes no spatial information beyond RGB and is completely unreliable for tracking limb positions, body orientation, or hand-object interactions in this sequence.
